facts.claim: ProjectSettingsHelper.cs was NOT touched by a recent change to the VirtualResolution code. `git log -3` on the file: 91fe384e (2026-10-06, AudioMixerAsset setting), 230f02d1 (2026-10-06, Master limiter setting), 5d048882 (2026-10-05, merge). `git log -S'ReadPositiveDimension'` gives only b07f3b5e (2026-10-03, 'feat(project): virtual resolution project setting (E19.s)'), which also created the test file. Re-verified.

The defect site, re-read: ProjectSettingsHelper.cs:97-106 is `ReadPositiveDimension(JObject declaration, string key)`; line 99 `int? value = (int?)declaration[key];` then `if (value is not > 0) throw new InvalidDataException($"Project setting 'VirtualResolution.{key}' must be a positive integer.")`. Width and Height go through it at lines 83-84; the non-object guard is at 78-81 (separate branch); Mode (86-92) does `(string)declaration["Mode"]`. Load parses the file with `JObject.Parse(File.ReadAllText(fileName))` (line 19), so a JSON integer arrives as a long (or BigInteger beyond long), a decimal literal as a double. Newtonsoft.Json 13.0.4 (Directory.Packages.props:19), net9.0 (Directory.Build.props). Missing key gives a C# null token; JSON null gives a JValue of type Null; both end at the existing message.

Byte-search reproduced: Newtonsoft.Json.dll 13.0.4 (net6.0) contains the int32 table {Integer=6, Float=7, String=8, Comment=5, Raw=13, Boolean=9} at offsets 708148, 708416 and 708448, a different table {Boolean, Integer, Float, String, Comment, Raw} once at 708244, and (UTF-16) the message 'Can not convert {0} to Int32.' once. This shows only that a number-type table accepting String, Float and Boolean exists; it does not bind that table to the `(int?)` operator, and the count of 3 does not map one-to-one to operators (a 7-entry table sharing the same 6-entry prefix may account for one). It is a byte search of Newtonsoft.Json.dll, NOT of ALUN_CD.EXE, and carries no decision weight on its own.

A reflective GPU route for the band clear exists in principle and was not examined by the discovery report: the repo has GpuFact/GpuDeviceHost (CasaEngine.Tests/UI/Backend/GpuDeviceHost.cs; HeadlessGame there is a plain MonoGame Game, not a CasaEngineGame; tests skip without a device), and the private field name `_graphicsDeviceService` is present in MonoGame.Framework 3.8.5.1 (DesktopGL) by byte search, so an uninitialised CasaEngineGame could in theory be given a device and ClearVirtualResolutionBands invoked by reflection. Rows: ("\"abc\"",Width), ("\"abc\"",Height), ("\"320\"",Width), ("\"320\"",Height), ("true",Width), ("true",Height), ("1.5",Width), ("1.5",Height), ("320.0",Width), ("{}",Height), ("[]",Width), plus the pin row ("null",Width). Save is not touched, so the converter's output (AlundraGame.json, written through ProjectSettingsHelper.Save with int properties) is byte-identical: no change to the export, the Alundra DLL or Alundra.Tests. After the bump, re-run the converter's ProjectWriterTests (alundra-casaengine-project-converter.Tests/ProjectWriterTests.cs reads the written file back through ProjectSettingsHelper.Load) and the engine CasaEngine.Tests, built explicitly because CasaEngine.Tests is outside the .sln (use `--blame-hang-timeout`). Direct execution without a new plan file is consistent with engine AGENTS.md:22 because G5 is already a slice of the triage and the engine part is a single commit; the pointer bump and the plan/backlog edit are bookkeeping in the parent repo.

Everything about the current behaviour per token (rounding of 1.5 to 2, true accepted as 1, strings accepted) is inferred from Json.NET source knowledge and a byte search of the DLL (which proves only that a String/Boolean-accepting number table exists), not executed. The red-first run is the real proof. The backlog and triage wording ('boolean throws', 'float truncated') is probably wrong on both points.
The production snippet and the tests were written without compiling (no dotnet allowed here). The patterns are valid C# 13 to the best of my reading; the build is the check.

Load mutates the settings property by property before throwing (WindowTitle, ProjectName, ... are already assigned when VirtualResolution fails), and WithCleanGlobals restores only VirtualResolution and ProjectPath. This is existing behaviour shared by the current failing-load tests; it is not made worse, but it is also not fixed here.

Adjacent issues (non-string or numeric Mode, DebugWidth/DebugHeight leniency) are left out on purpose, per engine AGENTS.md:15 (document, do not implement). If the author wants them, they are a second slice.
